newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Aug 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Aug 19.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Locally owned carrier Interair has suspended all its flights with immediate effect, citing fears for passenger safety as the reason.

- Wine co-operative KWV's statutory powers had allowed it to accumulate more than 800 million rand in assets, to which government might be entitled in the event of the co-operative's planned privatisation, it emerged in the Cape High Court on Monday.
- Defence Minister Joe Modise was not yet in control of the affairs of the defence department, defence secretary Pierre Steyn told Parliament's joint standing committee on defence on Monday.

- The Eastern Cape was badly hit by trade union federation Cosatu's 24 hour strike on Monday in support of demands on the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill, with 80 percent of workers heeding the call, employer organisations said.

- The SA software company which had been making and selling UK-based Dr Solomon's antivirus solutions under contract for the past eight years had been threatened with legal action which could force it to hand over its confidential customer database.
BUSINESS REPORT
- The JSE's all share index posted its seventh consecutive fall on Monday, losing 1,06 percent, or 78,5 points, to 7361,3 and joining the worldwide fright over Wall Street's losses.

- Ingwe, the world's largest steam coal exporter and part of the Billiton stable, pushed operating profit 35 percent higher to 1,43 billion rand in the year to June 30, despite depressed international coal prices this year, the company said on Monday.

- The net asset value of KWV, the wine co-operative, was just short of 2 billion rand, of which 800 billion rand belonged to the state, the Cape High Court heard on Monday at the resumption of KWV's attempt to get court sanction to convert from a co-operative to a public company.
- Southern Sun associate Tsogo Sun and Johnnic have drawn battle lines over the zoning rights associated with applications for casino licences in the Sandton-Midrand area
- How much money did Real Africa Asset Management, a joint venture between Sanlam and Real Africa Holdings, start off with. This is the 2 billion rand question.
SAKE BEELD

-- Tito Mboweni, Minister of Labour, has been given undertakings by Cosatu representatives on certain changes to the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill which will cause Cosatu to support the proposal.

- Ingwe Coal Corporation increased its attributable profit for the year to end June by 42 percent to 711,9 million rand. Earnings per share rose 37 percent to 320 cents and the dividend for the full year rose from 36 percent to 150 cents.
THE STAR

- Isaac Mofokeng, who hit national and international headlines when he came to grief in an enounter with Max the gorilla at Johannesburg Zoo, is a former policeman who has left his former colleagues red-faced after his brazen prison breakout last week.

- A close friend of Lawrie Fraser and a young Malawian national will spend the week behind bars on charges relating to the kidnapping of Fraser's son, Timothy Funnell, from his adoptive father's home in Malawi earlier this year.
